summary: Kenkai Naganuma (1883–1980) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served on the faculty at Kyushu University from circa 1926 to 1946 and held a post at Kurume University from circa 1950 to 1964.

Kennard Lipman worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completing doctoral studies under the supervision of Herbert V. Guenther. He has served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Historian and Indologist Kenneth Ballhatchet (1922–1995) studied at Clifton College and Peterhouse, Cambridge. He served as a Lecturer in the History of Modern India at SOAS from 1948 to 1988 and Reader in Indian History at Oxford from 1963 to 1965.

Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his doctoral studies at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University attested in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk, an Indologist and historian, studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his Ph.D. at Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He taught at Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen, alongside posts at UCLA, UW-Madison, and Toronto.

Kenneth J. Guest is a religious studies scholar and sinologist who studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY Graduate Center under Aloysius Pieris. He held academic appointments at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended Emmanuel College and studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. He held posts at Trinity College, YMCA College, Pacific School of Religion, and the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor of philosophy at the University at Buffalo, chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1996–1999), and chaired the Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai until 1999.

Kenneth K. S. Ch'en (1907–1993) studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, Yenching, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. A scholar of Chinese Buddhism, he held professorships at the Harvard-Yenching Institute, UCLA, and Princeton University.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Stanford, the Institute of Buddhist Studies, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held faculty positions at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Musashino University.
Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Somerled Macdonald (1832–1903) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He was educated at the University of Aberdeen and New College, Edinburgh, and held posts as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta and with the United Free Church Mission.

Kenneth W. Jones (1934–1996) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Stockton University and UC Berkeley under Thomas Metcalf. Beginning in 1965, he taught at Kansas State University, where he became a Distinguished Professor in 1989.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned literature doctorates at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Aichi Gakuin University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and became president of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who obtained a doctorate in literature from Otani University. He is an emeritus professor at Hanazono University, attested in 2014 and 2026.
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He pursued his education at Ryukoku University beginning in 1938 and later studied at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist and Tibetology scholar educated at Bukkyo University. He served as a professor at Koyasan University, Seizan College, and Shuchiin University, and was named professor emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He was educated at Otani University, where he was also attested as a professor in 2006.

Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued higher education at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He held an associate professorship at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College, attested between 2015 and 2016.

Kenyu Mitomo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his master's and doctorate at Rissho University and studied at UC Berkeley. He served from 1968 to 2015 at Rissho University, where he was Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies.
